cells.tense: The mind is resting here, on purpose, and the stillness holds.
cells.act: walk toward what connects, leaving what does not
cells.ask: Notice which conversations leave you clearer than they found you, and keep going toward those. Let one that doesn't, drop.
cells.core:
Step back and take in the whole of something — a household, a stretch of work, a year — and the shape of it comes without forcing. That's where you're sitting. Your mind has found quiet the same way, by settling into its bearings instead of pressing the noise down. Seeing what's true across a picture and letting the mind come to rest are one motion in you.

What takes effort is the upkeep. From that step back you can tell which ties still carry weight and which have gone hollow, and know it without doing anything about it. Walk toward what connects, and let one that doesn't drop. Nothing has to be announced or decided — one quiet letting-go, and the rest of the picture left as it is.

cells.tense: The mind is braced ahead of a future it cannot write in.
cells.act: keep the heading when it is contested
cells.ask: When someone questions where you're headed, say what it is once and stop. No next paragraph, no defense added on top.
cells.core:
You see the whole pattern, and it keeps moving. So the mind that could be resting from looking stays on watch instead — reading the shape ahead, reading it again, running back for the parts you missed. Looking at a pattern that carries its own stillness has been pointed forward, and rest thin enough to sleep through is the version you'll accept.

Come back to where seeing and resting were the same act, and not to the plan. When someone questions the direction you're holding, say what it is once, quietly, and stop there. The pattern can keep; you don't have to answer it every turn. Let the next move wait for its own turn.

cells.tense: The mind once rested, and it has not come back from there.
cells.act: let yourself be drawn before you choose
cells.ask: Follow what pulls at you — a voice, a window, a walk — a few minutes before deciding anything about it. The pull gets its turn first.
cells.core:
The whole picture still arrives — you take in the shape of a room on the way in, the way you have for as long as you can remember. What isn't arriving is the way it used to feel, the mind setting itself down once the read was done. You watch everything and let little touch you, and you describe it as staying calm. There's no charge in it. Nothing restful sits in that, and nothing is wrong with you either.

Start smaller than a decision. Follow what pulls at you — a voice, a window, a walk — a few minutes without picking it. Being drawn comes before choosing. Taking it all in gets its depth back from that, and the stillness comes along with it.

cells.tense: The mind is resting now, and no one is writing that down.
cells.act: cross over to the people it actually requires
cells.ask: When a moment of ease comes over you and someone asks how you got through it, say what settled you, plainly. Nothing more than that.
cells.core:
Watch you through a hard week and the pattern is plain: you get quieter, take in the whole of it, and start to settle. Ask what got you through, and the answer is nothing much, or the break, or that things aren't so bad. The calm is yours and it is doing the work — the account just leaves it out.

This has been going quietly for a while. Some part of you reads a room, takes it all in, and comes to rest without ever calling it by name. Don't file it as a report; let it be heard. Cross to the people who need to hear it, and say what truly settled you. Nothing gets fixed by the silence being kept.
